## Purpose and Entrypoints
OpenCode is an archived Go terminal AI coding assistant (continued elsewhere as Crush). The executable starts at `main.go`, with Cobra command setup and CLI/non-interactive prompt handling in `cmd/root.go`. A separate schema-generation command lives at `cmd/schema/main.go`.

## Application Composition
`internal/app/app.go` is the core composition layer: it initializes application services and connects configuration, persistence, LLM execution, UI, and runtime services. `internal/app/lsp.go` integrates language-server lifecycle into the app. The primary control boundary is interactive Bubble Tea TUI versus one-shot CLI prompt mode; both use the same underlying agent stack.

## Configuration and Persistent State
Configuration is loaded and merged from user/project locations by `internal/config/config.go` and initialized through `internal/config/init.go`. It controls provider credentials, agents/models, shell, MCP servers, LSP servers, data directory, and compaction behavior.

SQLite persistence is encapsulated by `internal/db/connect.go`, `internal/db/db.go`, and embedded migrations in `internal/db/migrations/`. Generated query layers store sessions, messages, and tracked files. Session/message domain behavior sits above this storage boundary in `internal/session/session.go` and `internal/message/message.go`.

## Agent and Model Execution
The agent loop in `internal/llm/agent/agent.go` turns user messages and prompt templates into model requests, streams or processes responses, invokes tools, and persists resulting conversation state. Agent-specific tool orchestration and MCP exposure are in `internal/llm/agent/agent-tool.go` and `internal/llm/agent/mcp-tools.go`.

Provider adapters normalize external model APIs behind `internal/llm/provider/provider.go`; concrete integrations include `internal/llm/provider/openai.go`, `internal/llm/provider/anthropic.go`, `internal/llm/provider/bedrock.go`, and others. Model catalogs/configuration are separated in `internal/llm/models/models.go`. This boundary supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Azure, Bedrock, Copilot, Groq, OpenRouter, Vertex AI, xAI, and OpenAI-compatible local endpoints.

## Prompt, Context, and Session Continuity
Prompt roles/templates are defined in `internal/llm/prompt/coder.go`, `internal/llm/prompt/task.go`, and `internal/llm/prompt/summarizer.go`. The system uses these for coding, delegated tasks, titles, and context compaction. Auto-compaction summarizes a near-limit conversation into a successor session, preserving usable context while avoiding provider context-window limits.

## Tooling, Permissions, and External Processes
Built-in tools are registered through `internal/llm/tools/tools.go`, with filesystem/code mutation and shell execution in `internal/llm/tools/{view,write,edit,patch,bash}.go`. Tools form the execution boundary between untrusted model requests and the local workspace. `internal/permission/permission.go` governs approvals; non-interactive mode auto-approves.

MCP servers extend the tool set via stdio or SSE, mediated by agent MCP integration. Shell commands use the configured shell. Network-capable tools include URL fetch and Sourcegraph search.

## TUI, Events, and Code Intelligence
The Bubble Tea interface is rooted at `internal/tui/tui.go`; page routing is in `internal/tui/page/`, and the chat interaction surface is in `internal/tui/components/chat/chat.go`. Dialogs cover permissions, sessions, commands, model selection, and settings. `internal/pubsub/broker.go` supplies internal event distribution between runtime services and UI.

LSP support is implemented by `internal/lsp/client.go`, `internal/lsp/transport.go`, and `internal/lsp/watcher/watcher.go`: configured local language-server subprocesses receive workspace/file updates, while the diagnostics tool exposes diagnostics to the agent.
